card.title: The time between booking a venue tour and arriving deserves a plan
card.series: Ad Leads Aren't Worse Than Referrals. They're Just Colder.
card.audience: Venue owners investing in visibility who want to carry a couple's interest through to the in-person tour.
card.why_selected: This is the strongest offer-led scene because it shows WIA considering the couple's experience and the venue's real schedule together. It gives LeadLock a clear role while preserving the owner's role in sales. Its central point is pre-tour interest, distinct from the recent content about visibility, attribution and time away from Instagram.
card.wia_in_action: WIA reviewed the inquiry-to-tour journey and asked about the venue's existing virtual-tour option. Whitney suggested an earlier phone or virtual connection for couples whose in-person visit was further away, and the team suggested a supplemental email with wedding footage and an invitation to ask questions. The ideas worked within the owner's tour schedule rather than asking her to add more tour hours. They were recommendations on the call, not changes already made.
card.why_it_matters: An owner may think, 'They've booked the tour, so now we'll send reminders.' This scene adds another question: what would help that couple stay interested and feel more familiar with the venue while they wait? It shows our view that follow-up should support the owner's own sales conversation, not replace it.
evidence_points: The WIA team proposed reviewing the language and personalization of nurture between inquiry and tour.
The venue owner said some couples schedule further ahead to accommodate family and described limits on when the venue can host tours.
Whitney asked whether virtual tours were already an option, and the owner said they were.
Whitney proposed an earlier personal connection; Fallon proposed a supplemental email for couples with a longer wait.
card.core_perspective: When a couple schedules a tour a few weeks away, there's an opportunity to help them picture their wedding before they arrive. We look at what happens during that wait, including the emails they receive and where a personal conversation would help.
card.offer_connection: Connect this to LeadLock and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage: WIA builds automated email and text follow-up that supports the owner's personal sales conversations. The scene makes the value of pre-consult nurture concrete without presenting the proposed virtual contact or supplemental email as an implemented feature. Close the Instagram piece with an invitation to inquire about LeadLock.
verify_before_publishing: Approve an anonymized account of this historical call; credit Whitney's suggestion and do not present Fallon as current staff.
Keep both follow-up ideas as recommendations, with no cancellation figures, implementation claims or results.

prior_content_context.argument: When a couple schedules a tour a few weeks away, there's an opportunity to help them picture their wedding before they arrive. We look at what happens during that wait, including the emails they receive and where a personal conversation would help.
prior_content_context.audience: Venue owners investing in visibility who want to carry a couple's interest through to the in-person tour.
prior_content_context.mechanism: WIA reviewed the inquiry-to-tour journey and asked about the venue's existing virtual-tour option. Whitney proposed an earlier phone or virtual connection for couples whose in-person visit was further away. Fallon Looney, who was on the historical call and is no longer with WIA, suggested a supplemental email with wedding footage and an invitation to ask questions. The recommendations respected the owner's tour schedule rather than asking her to add more tour hours.

prior_content_context.argument: I want to understand what a couple was weighing when they chose your business. Their review can tell us what they loved about the experience. Asking about the booking decision can give us different information to consider when we write your ads.
prior_content_context.audience: Wedding pros with strong reviews who want their advertising to reflect why their best-fit couples chose them.
prior_content_context.mechanism: During a strategy call, Whitney explained that WIA asks ELEVATE clients for existing buying research. She proposed collecting feedback from newly booked couples and using what WIA learns to inform ad copy and landing pages. The WIA move is customer research tied to a specific advertising decision.

prior_content_context.argument: We want enough evidence to make a useful recommendation. In office hours, Carmen considered how much traffic a venue campaign had received, looked at what visitors were doing after the click and recommended Jacqueline's feedback on the landing page. She kept the open questions open.
prior_content_context.audience: Wedding venue owners who want expert guidance on what to keep running, what to review and when to make a change.
prior_content_context.mechanism: Carmen used diagnosis beyond the dashboard. She considered the limited traffic, discussed different kinds of visitor behavior and avoided claiming a cause. When a visitor reached the inquiry form and then moved away, she recommended asking Jacqueline for landing-page feedback. The scene shows support that includes judgment and collaboration, even before there is a settled answer.
